es.summary: Bloqueo parcial o total del colon que impide el paso del contenido intestinal, pudiendo deberse a diverticulitis, fecaloma, tumor o vólvulo. Produce distensión, dolor y riesgo de isquemia intestinal.
key_points: Obstrucción mecánica vs funcional del colon
Dolor abdominal colico y distensión son signos tempranos
Radiografía y TAC confirman nivel de obstrucción
Manejo inicial incluye hidratación, descompresión y cirugía
Complicaciones graves: perforación, peritonitis y sepsis

pathophysiology: Obstrucción mecánica impide el tránsito del bolo fecal
Aumento de presión intraluminal reduce perfusión mucosa
Isquemia prolongada lleva a necrosis y perforación
Respuesta inflamatoria aumenta edema y empeora la obstrucción
signs_symptoms: Dolor abdominal tipo cólico, empeora después de comer
Náuseas y vómitos, a veces biliosos
Ausencia de gases y heces (obstrucción completa)
Taquicardia y presión arterial baja si hay compromiso sistémico
diagnostics: Radiografía de abdomen: niveles de aire‑líquido y distensión
Tomografía axial computarizada: localiza nivel y causa
Electrolitos: hipopotasemia o hipernatremia por pérdidas
Pruebas de función renal: creatinina ↑ si hay deshidratación
treatment: Analgesia con opioides o AINE según indicación
Antibióticos de amplio espectro si se sospecha perforación o peritonitis
Cirugía (colectomía o resección) si obstrucción completa o complicaciones
nursing_care: Evaluar dolor, distensión y patrón de eliminación cada 2 h
Monitorear signos vitales, especialmente TA y FC
Registrar salida de líquidos y balance hídrico
patient_teaching: Promover actividad física moderada para estimular motilidad intestinal
Instruir sobre signos de recaída: dolor intenso, vómitos persistentes

outcomes: Balance hídrico: ingreso neto ≥0 mL en 24 h
Presión arterial estabilizada >100/70 mmHg en 12 h
Hidratación adecuada: piel húmeda y turgencia normal

interventions.action: Administrar solución cristaloide IV según orden y registrar velocidad
interventions.rationale: Restablece el volumen intravascular y previene shock hipovolémico

interventions.action: Monitorear balance hídrico cada 2 h y reportar déficit >500 mL
interventions.rationale: Permite detectar rápidamente la necesidad de reposición adicional

interventions.action: Evaluar signos de perfusión periférica (capilaridad, temperatura)
Educar al paciente sobre la importancia de la hidratación oral cuando sea permitido
interventions.rationale: Facilita la transición a hidratación oral y previene recaídas

evidenced_by: Limitación para movilizarse fuera de la cama
Fatiga al intentar cambiar de posición
outcomes: Paciente tolera movilización a silla 30 min sin aumento de dolor en 48 h
Frecuencia respiratoria <22 rpm durante actividad ligera

interventions.action: Planificar movilización gradual: primero en cama, luego silla, luego deambulación corta
interventions.rationale: Previene agotamiento y mejora la tolerancia al ejercicio

interventions.action: Administrar analgesia antes de la actividad según prescripción
interventions.rationale: Control del dolor permite mayor participación en la movilización

interventions.action: Enseñar técnicas de respiración diafragmática durante el movimiento
interventions.rationale: Reduce dolor y mejora la oxigenación

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de dolor antes y después de cada sesión y ajustar plan
interventions.rationale: Asegura que la actividad sea segura y bien tolerada

en.summary: Partial or complete blockage of the colon that prevents intestinal contents from passing, which may be due to diverticulitis, fecaloma, tumor, or volvulus. It causes distension, pain, and risk of intestinal ischemia.
key_points: Colicky abdominal pain and distension are early signs
X‑ray and CT confirm obstruction level
Initial management includes hydration, decompression, and surgery
Severe complications: perforation, peritonitis, and sepsis

pathophysiology: Mechanical obstruction blocks fecal bolus transit
Intraluminal pressure rise reduces mucosal perfusion
Prolonged ischemia leads to necrosis and perforation
Inflammatory response increases edema and worsens obstruction
signs_symptoms: Colicky abdominal pain, worsens after eating
Absence of gas and stool (complete obstruction)
Tachycardia and low blood pressure if systemic compromise
diagnostics: Abdominal X‑ray: air‑fluid levels and distension
Computed tomography: localizes level and cause
Electrolytes: hypokalemia or hypernatremia from losses
Renal function tests: creatinine ↑ if dehydration
treatment: Analgesia with opioids or NSAIDs as indicated
Broad‑spectrum antibiotics if perforation or peritonitis suspected
Surgery (colectomy or resection) if complete obstruction or complications
nursing_care: Assess pain, distension, and elimination pattern every 2 h
Monitor vital signs, especially BP and HR
Record fluid output and fluid balance
patient_teaching: Encourage moderate physical activity to stimulate intestinal motility
Teach signs of recurrence: intense pain, persistent vomiting

outcomes: Fluid balance: net intake ≥0 mL in 24 h
Blood pressure stabilized >100/70 mmHg in 12 h
Adequate hydration: skin moist and normal turgor

interventions.action: Administer IV crystalloid solution per order and record rate
interventions.rationale: Restores intravascular volume and prevents hypovolemic shock

interventions.action: Monitor fluid balance every 2 h and report deficit >500 mL
interventions.rationale: Allows rapid detection of need for additional replacement

interventions.action: Assess peripheral perfusion signs (capillary refill, temperature)
Educate patient on importance of oral hydration when permitted
interventions.rationale: Facilitates transition to oral intake and prevents relapse

evidenced_by: Limited ability to mobilize out of bed
outcomes: Patient tolerates chair mobilization for 30 min without increased pain in 48 h
Respiratory rate <22 rpm during light activity

interventions.action: Plan gradual mobilization: bed, then chair, then short ambulation
interventions.rationale: Prevents exhaustion and improves exercise tolerance

interventions.action: Administer analgesia before activity per prescription
interventions.rationale: Pain control allows greater participation in mobilization

interventions.action: Teach diaphragmatic breathing techniques during movement
Assess pain level before and after each session and adjust plan
interventions.rationale: Ensures activity is safe and well tolerated

sources.name: Medical-Surgical Nursing: Disorders of the Lower GI System

summary.0.quote: An intestinal obstruction is a partial or complete blockage of the intestines so that contents of the intestine cannot pass through.

key_points.4.quote: Perforation causes the spilling of bacteria and bowel contents into the peritoneal cavity, causing a contained abscess or peritonitis.

sections.pathophysiology.2.quote: This creates an inflammatory response, which can lead to local ischemia and perforation.

sections.signs_symptoms.4.quote: Vital signs should be completed with a focus on blood pressure and heart rate, especially in the patient having diarrhea, to evaluate for signs of dehydration, such as tachycardia and hypotension.

sections.diagnostics.0.quote: Abnormal findings (e.g., air-fluid levels, dilated loops of bowel, free air under the diaphragm) may indicate pathology.

sections.diagnostics.3.quote: Dehydration can lead to electrolyte disturbances, particularly hypernatremia.

sections.complications.1.quote: Perforation causes the spilling of bacteria and bowel contents into the peritoneal cavity, causing a contained abscess or peritonitis.

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: Vital signs should be completed with a focus on blood pressure and heart rate, especially in the patient having diarrhea, to evaluate for signs of dehydration, such as tachycardia and hypotension.

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: The nurse evaluates trends in the patient’s intake and output, vital signs, and electrolytes to assess care.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: Nurses encourage patients to engage in regular physical activity because exercise can stimulate bowel motility and promote regular bowel movements.
